stem: Draw the straight line through $A({=x1}, {=y1})$ and $B({=x2}, {=y2})$.
solution: Find the gradient between A and B: m = (y2 − y1) / (x2 − x1).
Keep the sign of each difference exactly as it comes out — do not drop a sign when a coordinate is already negative.
Starting from A, step according to that gradient (rise over run) to fix the line's direction.
Any two points lying on this same line are an acceptable construction — it is the line itself that is graded, not the two named points.
notes: Tests the geometric core of LO1 (the unique line two points determine) rather than the symbolic y = mx + c form; graded on the property (any two collinear points are correct, FR-1205). Anchor ex8-6-10a's own points (A(-6,1)) fall outside the instrument's ±5 lattice limit, so instance parameters were rescaled to the same gradient family (1/3) while two further instances stress negative coordinates and a whole-number gradient. intercept-wrong and vertical-line are valid predicates for this kind but have no clean, non-strained match among this LO's own misconceptions, so they are left undiagnosed rather than forced.
